title: The Two Sons
text:
In the temple courts in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders challenged Jesus about his authority. According to Matthew's Gospel, he answered them with a short parable.

A man had two sons. He went to the first and said, "Son, go and work in the vineyard today." The son answered, "I will not." But later he changed his mind and went.

Then the father went to the second son and said the same thing. That son answered, "I will, sir," but he did not go.

Jesus asked his listeners which of the two did what his father wanted. "The first," they said.

Jesus then applied the story to them. Tax collectors and prostitutes, he said, were entering the kingdom of God ahead of them. John the Baptist had come showing them the way of righteousness, and they had not believed him, while the tax collectors and prostitutes did. Even after seeing that, they had not changed their minds and believed.
lesson: What a child does matters more than what he promises. The same is true of adults: a polite yes followed by nothing is worse than an honest no that turns into action.
people: A father, two sons, Jesus, the chief priests and elders
